# omada_firewall_acl_order (Resource)

Controls the **evaluation order** of firewall ACL rules. Omada evaluates gateway ACLs top to bottom and the first match wins, so a permit below a deny that also matches is dead. A created rule always appends to the end of the list, which makes that the default outcome.

The listed rules are arranged into this relative order **among the positions they already occupy**. Rules at positions 2, 5 and 7 can be rearranged among 2, 5 and 7, and nothing else on the controller moves — so a config need not account for rules it does not manage. The flip side is that a rule cannot be moved past a rule that is not listed; to do that, list that rule too. Listing every rule of the type gives complete control of the order.

One instance per site and ACL type. `rule_ids` is an order, not a set: changing it updates in place, and destroying the resource stops managing the order without changing it on the controller.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Omada evaluates gateway ACLs top to bottom and the first match wins, and a
# newly created rule always APPENDS to the end of the list. So a deny created
# before the permits that should override it ends up above them, silently
# shadowing both — the rules all exist, look correct, and do the wrong thing.
#
# This resource asserts the evaluation order.

resource "omada_firewall_acl" "permit_frigate_wan" {
  name            = "Permit Frigate to WAN"
  policy          = "permit"
  source_type     = 1 # IP group
  source_ids      = [var.frigate_group_id]
  destination_ids = [var.any_group_id]
  direction       = { lan_to_lan = false, lan_to_wan = true }
}

resource "omada_firewall_acl" "permit_nvr_wan" {
  name            = "Permit NVR to WAN"
  policy          = "permit"
  source_type     = 1
  source_ids      = [var.nvr_group_id]
  destination_ids = [var.any_group_id]
  direction       = { lan_to_lan = false, lan_to_wan = true }
}

resource "omada_firewall_acl" "deny_cameras_wan" {
  name            = "Deny Cameras to WAN"
  policy          = "deny"
  source_type     = 0 # LAN network — the whole camera VLAN
  source_ids      = [var.cameras_network_id]
  destination_ids = [var.any_group_id]
  direction       = { lan_to_lan = false, lan_to_wan = true }
}

# The two permits must evaluate BEFORE the deny, or the cameras VLAN loses its
# exceptions and Frigate stops getting image pulls while detection carries on
# working — a failure that looks like nothing happened.
resource "omada_firewall_acl_order" "gateway" {
  rule_ids = [
    omada_firewall_acl.permit_frigate_wan.id,
    omada_firewall_acl.permit_nvr_wan.id,
    omada_firewall_acl.deny_cameras_wan.id,
  ]
}

# Reading the current order: the data source lists each type in evaluation
# order and exposes `index`.
data "omada_firewall_acls" "all" {}

output "gateway_acl_order" {
  value = [
    for a in data.omada_firewall_acls.all.acls : "${a.index}: ${a.name}"
    if a.type == "gateway"
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `rule_ids` (List of String) ACL rule IDs in the order they should be evaluated, first match first. Reference the rules rather than hardcoding IDs (`omada_firewall_acl.x.id`) so Terraform creates them before ordering them.

### Optional

- `site` (String) Site name. Defaults to the primary site. Changing this forces replacement.
- `type` (String) ACL type. Only `gateway` is accepted: `modifyIndex` has been verified live for gateway ACLs only, and switch and EAP ACLs are not yet supported. Changing forces replacement.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) `<site_id>/<type>` — the order is a per-site, per-type singleton.
- `site_id` (String)

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The order is a per-site, per-type singleton, so the ACL type is the whole ID.
terraform import omada_firewall_acl_order.gateway gateway

# On a non-default site, prefix the site name:
terraform import omada_firewall_acl_order.gateway 'Branch Office/gateway'

# The import brings in no rule_ids -- which rules a configuration intends to
# order is not discoverable from the controller -- so expect a one-time diff
# that adds them.
```
